subject: hospitality-tourism
intro: Travel and tourism leads to the people-facing side of one of the world's largest industries — running hotels, restaurants and tours, planning events and selling journeys.

roles.title: Lodging Managers
roles.what: Plan, direct and coordinate the operations of hotels, resorts and other accommodation providers, managing front-office work, guest services, budgets and the staff who keep the property running.
roles.where: The customer service unit — delivering and providing service for different types of tourists — is the manager's daily craft, and the global tourism unit's features of destinations explains who the guests are and what they expect.

roles.title: Food Service Managers
roles.what: Plan, direct and coordinate the activities of restaurants and other establishments that serve food and beverages, from staffing and ordering through to service standards and customer complaints.
roles.where: The unit on skills required when working in the travel and tourism industry and the whole customer service strand — service delivery, handling different customer types — map straight onto running a food operation.

roles.title: Travel Agents
roles.what: Plan and sell transportation and accommodation for customers: match destinations and transport modes to budgets and dates, build itineraries, sell tour packages and resolve travel problems.
roles.where: Types of tourism and the reasons people travel, the different types of transport and their appeal, and customer service provision for different types of tourists are the exact matching work an agent does all day.

roles.title: Meeting, Convention, and Event Planners
roles.what: Coordinate the activities of staff, venue personnel and clients to arrange group meetings, events and conventions — site selection, logistics, budgets and the programme itself.
roles.where: Destination marketing — market research and analysis, market segmentation and targeting, the marketing mix — is how planners position events, and the organisations unit explains the partnerships that make large events work.

roles.title: Tour Guides and Escorts
roles.what: Escort individuals or groups on sightseeing tours and through places of interest, describing the sights, managing the group's pace and bringing destinations to life for visitors.
roles.where: The features of destinations and their appeal to different tourists, and the managing destinations sustainably unit — economic, environmental and sociocultural impacts — give guides the interpretation their commentary draws on.
